349291.title: The zero-sum 5-flow conjecture for non-symmetric designs
349291.statement:
A $t$-$(v,k,\lambda)$ design $\mathcal{D}=(X,\mathcal{B})$ consists of a $v$-element point set $X$ and a collection of $k$-subsets of $X$, called blocks, such that every $t$-subset of $X$ lies in exactly $\lambda$ blocks. The design is **non-symmetric** when its number of blocks differs from its number of points. A **zero-sum $n$-flow** of $\mathcal{D}$ is a map

$$
f:\mathcal{B}\longrightarrow \{\pm1,\ldots,\pm(n-1)\}
$$

such that the sum of the values over all blocks incident with each point is zero. **The zero-sum 5-flow conjecture.** Every non-symmetric design admits a zero-sum $5$-flow. The conjecture was presented in the source as one of two conjectures appearing in earlier work; no resolution is supplied here.

349420.title: Characterization of graphs for which the blow-up optimization is unattained
349420.statement:
Let $H$ be a graph with no isolated vertices, let $k$ be a positive integer, and let $\beta(H,k)$ be the optimization parameter defined in the paper. **Attainment conjecture for $\beta(H,k)$.** The quantity $\beta(H,k)$ is not achieved if and only if $k=1$ and either $H=K_{1,m}$ or $H=mK_2$ for some $m\geq 2$, where $mK_2$ is the matching on $m$ edges.

The paper notes that the two listed families are known never to attain the optimum, whereas $\beta(H,k)$ is attained whenever $k\delta(H)\geq 2$. The conjecture proposes that these are the only exceptions.

349472.title: Conjecture on uniformly signed 6-cycles in bipartite planar graphs
349472.statement:
Let $G$ be a bipartite planar graph of girth at least $6$, and let $\sigma$ be a signature on $G$, assigning a sign to every edge. Say that the **6-cycles have the same sign** when every cycle of length $6$ in the signed graph $(G,\sigma)$ has the same sign. **Uniform-sign 6-cycle conjecture.** Then $(G,\sigma)$ admits a homomorphism to the negatively signed $4$-cycle $C_{-4}$.

This proposed condition generalizes the four-color-theorem reformulation and includes the role of the negative-girth result discussed in the paper. It is presented as a conjecture after the paper's theorem on signed bipartite planar graphs of negative girth at least $8$; no resolution is supplied in the given text.

349555.title: Algebraicity characterization for rank-three Dowling geometries
349555.statement: Let $\Gamma$ be a nontrivial finite group, and let $p$ be a prime. **Dowling-geometry algebraicity conjecture.** The matroid $\operatorname{DG}(3,\Gamma)$ is algebraic over $\operatorname{GF}(p)$ if and only if there is some integer $j\ge 1$ such that $\Gamma$ is a subgroup of $\mathbb Z_{p^j-1}$. This is the analogous conjecture for Dowling geometries and would contribute to characterizing the fields over which these geometries are algebraic. The source does not give a resolution; the conjecture remains open.

349589.title: Neumann Lara's conjecture on oriented planar graph dichromatic number
349589.statement:
Let an **oriented graph** be a digraph obtained from a simple graph by orienting every edge, replacing it by exactly one of the two possible arcs between its end-vertices. A digraph is **$k$-dicolourable** if its vertex set can be partitioned into $k$ subsets inducing acyclic subdigraphs; its dichromatic number is the least such integer $k$. A planar graph is an oriented graph whose underlying graph is planar.

**Neumann Lara's conjecture.** Every oriented planar graph is $2$-dicolourable.

This conjecture is presented as an analogue of Grötzsch's theorem, which states that every triangle-free planar graph is $3$-colourable. The source provides no resolution status for the conjecture.

349809.title: Submodularity criterion for a unique maximal matroid
349809.statement: Let $\mathcal X$ be a family of subsets of a finite set $E$, and let $\operatorname{val}_{\mathcal X}$ be the set function defined from proper $\mathcal X$-sequences. Suppose there is at least one $\mathcal X$-matroid on $E$. **Submodularity criterion.** The poset of all $\mathcal X$-matroids on $E$ has a unique maximal element if and only if $\operatorname{val}_{\mathcal X}$ is a submodular set function on $E$. More generally, without assuming that an $\mathcal X$-matroid exists, the poset of all $\mathcal X$-cyclic matroids on $E$ should have a unique maximal element if and only if $\operatorname{val}_{\mathcal X}$ is submodular. The forward implication is supplied by the preceding lemma; the converse is the conjectural part, while the more general cyclic formulation is also proposed.

349818.title: Hermitian forms graph smallest eigenvalue conjectures
349818.statement:
Let $Q_q(d)$ be the Hermitian forms scheme on the $d\times d$ Hermitian matrices over $\mathbb{F}_{q^2}$, and let $Q_j(i)$ denote the eigenvalue indexed by $i$ in its distance-$j$ graph, for $0\leq i,j\leq d$.

**Hermitian forms eigenvalue conjectures.** (i) If $j$ is odd, then

$$
Q_j(1) \leq Q_j(i)
$$

for $0\leq i\leq d$. (ii) If $j$ is even and $j\geq 2$, then

$$
Q_j(d-j+2) \leq Q_j(i)
$$

for $0\leq i\leq d$.

Both assertions are proved in the paper for $q\geq 2$, $d\geq 6$, and $j\geq 1$.

349819.title: Hermitian forms graph absolute eigenvalue conjecture
349819.statement:
Let $Q_q(d)$ be the Hermitian forms scheme on the $d\times d$ Hermitian matrices over $\mathbb{F}_{q^2}$, and let $Q_j(i)$ denote the eigenvalue indexed by $i$ in its distance-$j$ graph.

**Hermitian absolute eigenvalue conjecture.** Let $d\geq 3$. Then

$$
|Q_j(i)| < |Q_j(1)|
$$

for $2\leq i\leq d$.

The theorem in the paper proves this assertion under the stated Hermitian-forms hypotheses, so it is resolved there.

349855.title: Nearly-ladder dual-graph counting conjecture for order polytopes
349855.statement: Assume $J(Q_{\mathbf{w}})=\widehat{P}(\mathbf{w})$, where $\mathbf{w}=varepsilon L R^{n-2}$ and $ngeq 3$. Consider triangulations of $\mathcal{O}(Q_{\mathbf{w}})$ and their dual graphs, and compare them with the dual graph of the canonical triangulation. **Nearly-ladder counting conjecture.** The number of triangulations whose dual graph is isomorphic to the dual graph of the canonical triangulation is $4n(n-2)!$. The paper reports verification for $n=3,4,5,6,7$; the assertion is otherwise open.

349948.title: The conjecture on the unique minimizer of normalized distance-Laplacian spectral radius
349948.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected graph on $n\geq 2$ vertices, let $K_n$ be the complete graph, and let $\rho(\mathcal D^{\mathcal L}(G))$ denote the spectral radius of the normalized distance Laplacian. **Unique-minimizer conjecture.**

$$
\rho\left(\mathcal D^{\mathcal L}(G)\right)=\frac{n}{n-1}
$$

if and only if $G$ is the complete graph $K_n$.

The lower bound and the corresponding normalized distance-Laplacian spectrum are known, but uniqueness of the minimizer had not been shown in the survey; the conjecture proposes that only $K_n$ attains equality.

349953.title: Real-rootedness of the Eulerian transformation on the binomial basis cone
349953.statement:
Let $n\geq 0$, and let $f$ be a polynomial of the form

$$
f=\sum_{k=0}^n a_k t^k(1+t)^{n-k},\qquad a_k\geq 0\quad(0\leq k\leq n).
$$

Let $\operatorname*{\mathcal E}:\mathbb{R}[t]\to\mathbb{R}[t]$ be the Eulerian transformation defined by $\operatorname*{\mathcal E}(t^m)=A_m(t)$, where $A_m(t)$ is the $m$-th Eulerian polynomial. **The paper's conjecture.** The polynomial $\operatorname*{\mathcal E}(f)$ is real-rooted.

This conjecture seeks a restricted real-rootedness-preservation property after Brenti's broader conjecture was disproved. The paper provides partial evidence, including alternatingly increasing and hence unimodal coefficients for the transformed polynomials, as well as real-rootedness results for important subfamilies; the full assertion remains open in the supplied text.

356832.title: NP-completeness of minimal queen completion on chessboards
356832.statement:
Let $n$ be a positive integer and let $Q$ be a set of $k$ queens placed on an $n\times n$ chessboard. For a nonnegative integer $l$, the minimal chessboard domination queen completion problem asks whether there is a set $Q'$ of size $k+l$ such that $Q\subset Q'$ and $Q'$ dominates the chessboard.

**Chessboard queen completion conjecture.** The minimal chessboard domination queen completion problem is NP-complete.

The problem concerns completing a prescribed partial queen placement to a dominating placement with a specified increase in size. The paper presents the claim as an open conjecture and does not provide a proof of NP-completeness.

357056.title: Existence of tight irreducible affine vector space partitions from divisible dimensions
357056.statement: Let $n$ be a positive integer, let $q$ be a prime power, and let $k$ be an integer with $1<k<n$ such that $k$ divides $n$. An affine vector space partition is a partition of the points of an affine space into affine subspaces; it is **tight** when its members have the prescribed uniform intersection properties, and **irreducible** when no two members lie in a common proper projective subspace. **Existence conjecture.** For each integer $1<k<n$ that divides $n$, there exists a tight irreducible affine vector space partition $\mathcal{U}$ of $\operatorname{PG}(n-1,q)$ of type $k^m$, where $m=q^{n-k}$. This would extend the preceding construction from the case $k=n/2$ to every proper divisor $k$ of $n$; the supplied text gives no proof or status evidence for the assertion.

358860.title: Cui–Hu conjecture on two abundant elements
358860.statement: Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a finite family of sets that is **union-closed**, meaning that the union of any two members belongs to $\mathcal{F}$. Suppose that every set in $\mathcal{F}$ has size at least $2$. **Cui–Hu conjecture.** There exist at least two elements such that each belongs to more than half of the sets in $\mathcal{F}$. This stronger assertion would imply Frankl's union-closed sets conjecture. It remains open according to the source, which presents it as a conjecture by Cui and Hu.

365728.title: Hocquard–Lajou–Luar conjecture for subcubic planar graphs
365728.statement: For a sequence $S=(s_1,dots,s_k)$ of non-decreasing positive integers, an $S$-packing edge-coloring of a graph $G$ is a partition of $E(G)$ into $E_1,dots,E_k$ such that the distance between any two distinct edges in $E_i$ is at least $s_i+1$. In particular, a $(1,2^6)$-coloring has one matching and six induced matchings, while a $(1^2,2^3)$-coloring has two matchings and three induced matchings. **Hocquard–Lajou–Luar's conjecture.** Every subcubic planar graph is $(1,2^6)$-packing edge-colorable and $(1^2,2^3)$-packing edge-colorable. These bounds concern intermediate edge-colorings between proper and strong edge-colorings. The conjecture is open in the supplied source context.

368604.title: Fields conjecture on the symmetric-group module structure of the superspace coinvariant ring
368604.statement:
Let $\Omega_n$ be the superspace ring with diagonal $\mathfrak{S}_n$-action, let $SR_n=\Omega_n/SI_n$ be its superspace coinvariant ring, and let $\mathbb{F}[\mathcal{OP}_n]$ be the permutation module on ordered set partitions of $[n]$. Let $\operatorname{sign}$ denote the one-dimensional sign representation of $\mathfrak{S}_n$. **Fields conjecture on the module structure.** There is an isomorphism of ungraded $\mathfrak{S}_n$-modules

$$
SR_n\cong_{\mathfrak{S}_n}\mathbb{F}[\mathcal{OP}_n]\otimes_{\mathbb{F}}\operatorname{sign}.
$$

This is one of the Fields Conjectures, asserting that the ungraded representation carried by the superspace coinvariant ring is modeled by ordered set partitions, with a sign twist. The supplied text gives no resolution status.

381752.title: The bipartite multiplicity Ryser-Brualdi-Stein conjecture
381752.statement:
Let $G$ be a complete bipartite graph on $2n$ vertices whose edge set is decomposed into perfect matchings $M_i$, for $i=1,\ldots,n$. Let $a_i$, for $i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}$, be non-negative integers satisfying

$$
\sum_{i=1}^n a_i=n-1.
$$

**Multiplicity Ryser-Brualdi-Stein conjecture.** There exists a matching $M$ in $G$ such that

$$
|M\cap M_i|=a_i\qquad\text{for each }i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}.
$$

This is presented as a multiplicity version of the Ryser-Brualdi-Stein conjecture. It would strengthen the three-colour bipartite conclusion to any number of colours and is open in the source. Noga Alon independently asked this question.

381915.title: Sturm-unimodality conjecture for refined Narayana polynomials
381915.statement: Let $W_{n,k}(t)$ be the polynomials considered in the paper. A finite sequence of real-rooted polynomials is Sturm-unimodal if it increases by interlacing up to one index and then decreases by reverse interlacing. **Sturm-unimodality conjecture.** For any fixed $n\geq 1$, the sequence $\{W_{n,k}(t)\}_{1\leq k\leq n}$ is Sturm-unimodal. This is a stronger interlacing property than coefficient or value unimodality, and remains conjectural in the source.

381930.title: The compatibility-count conjecture for $(3,n)$ generalized Feynman diagrams
381930.statement:
Let a $(3,n)$ generalized Feynman diagram (GFD) be a combinatorial object compatible with color orderings in the sense of the paper. **Compatibility-count conjecture.** Every $(3,n)$ GFD is compatible with exactly

$$
2^{2(n-4)}
$$

color orderings. This is motivated by the complete enumeration through $(3,8)$, where every GFD has the predicted number of compatible generalized color orderings; the assertion is proposed for general $n$.

381980.title: Conjectured initial values of the ML-degree polynomial
381980.statement:
Let $\phi(n,d)$ denote the polynomial that gives the dimension of the space of quadrics in $n$ variables passing through $d$ general points and tangent to $\binom{n+1}{2}-d-1$ general hyperplanes. **Initial-value conjecture.**

$$
\phi(0,d)=(-1)^{d-1},\qquad \phi(-1,d)=(-2)^{d-1}.
$$

These formulas extend the enumerative-geometric polynomial $\phi(n,d)$ to the initial nonpositive values $n=0$ and $n=-1$, following the program of combinatorial reciprocity. The source notes that these formulas were previously conjectured; their resolution is not established in the supplied context.
